symbols.name: G
symbols.space: A graph on \(V\) whose bidirected districts are cliques.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: The number of bidirected districts of \(G\).

symbols.name: R_j
symbols.def: A member is a tuple of deterministic response tables for all vertices in district \(D_j\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: The joint root law is the product \(\bigotimes_{j=1}^m\theta_j\).

symbols.name: ev_x
symbols.def: Evaluate the response tables in order \(\prec\), replacing the equations for \(X\) by the constants \(x\); \(\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}\) denotes factual evaluation.

symbols.name: P
symbols.role: Generic law on the relative interior of the supplied face.

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.role: A solution of \(\lambda B=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\), when one exists.

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.role: Fixed distance from the boundary of the support face.

symbols.name: sigma_min
symbols.role: Uniform lower bound for standard deviations.

symbols.name: G_bow
symbols.def: The binary bow graph \(X\to Y\) and \(X\leftrightarrow Y\).

symbols.name: G_IV
symbols.def: The binary instrumental-variable graph \(Z\to X\to Y\) and \(X\leftrightarrow Y\).

standard.name: Feasibility of the canonical discrete SCM constraints

definitions.name: First forbidden extensions
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_i(S)=\{(w,a):w\in S^{\le i-1},\ a\in\mathcal X_i,\ wa\notin S^{\le i}\}\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

definitions.name: District prefix indicator
definitions.construction: \(b_j^k(w,r_j)=\prod_{\ell\le k:\,V_\ell\in D_j}\mathbf 1\{r_{j,\ell}(w_{\operatorname{pa}_G(V_\ell)})=w_\ell\}\) for \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), \(w\in\prod_{\ell=1}^k\mathcal X_\ell\), and \(r_j\in\mathcal R_j\), with the empty product equal to one.

definitions.name: First-forbidden-prefix saturated local support
definitions.construction: \(T_j(S)=\{r_j\in\mathcal R_j:b_j^i(wa,r_j)=0\ \text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\text{ with }V_i\in D_j\text{ and every }(w,a)\in\mathcal F_i(S)\}\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

definitions.name: Supported district signature matrix
definitions.construction: For rows \(a\in\{0\}\cup S\) and columns \(r_j\in T_j(S)\), set \(B_j[0,r_j]=1\) and \(B_j[s,r_j]=b_j^n(s,r_j)\) for \(s\in S\).

definitions.name: Positive-prefix observable district signature
definitions.construction: Set \(t_j(P)[0]=1\) and \(t_j(P)[s]=\prod_{i:\,V_i\in D_j}P(V_{\le i}=s_{\le i})/P(V_{<i}=s_{<i})\) for every \(s\in S\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

definitions.name: Tensor district signature matrix
definitions.construction: \(B=\bigotimes_{j=1}^mB_j\), with columns indexed by \(T(S)\) and rows indexed by \((\{0\}\cup S)^m\).

definitions.name: Face-positive common denominator
definitions.construction: \(D_S(P)=\prod_{i=1}^n\prod_{w\in S^{\le i-1}}P(V_{<i}=w)\), where the empty-prefix factor equals one.

definitions.name: Saturated-face influence function
definitions.construction: \(\phi_P(s)=\partial F_{\lambda}(P)/\partial P(s)-\sum_{u\in S}P(u)\,\partial F_{\lambda}(P)/\partial P(u)\) for \(s\in S\).

definitions.name: Support-scoped compiler handle
definitions.construction: Handle: enrich do-search states with exact prefix domains and signed rational arrays, use the support-saturated matrices \(B_j\) as semantic invariants, and normalize a successful derivation by applying rootwise rational projectors onto \(\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B_j)\) before extracting a common denominator.

statements.statement: Assume \(S\) is realizable. Every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\) satisfies \(\operatorname{supp}(\theta_j)\subseteq T_j(S)\) for all \(j\). Every \(r\in T(S)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(r)\in S\), and \(\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(T(S))=S\). Consequently, every product law strictly positive on each \(T_j(S)\) has factual support exactly \(S\), and \(T(S)\) is the unique largest Cartesian response support among all members of \(\Theta_S\).
statements.justification: This removes chart ambiguity before any identifying formula is constructed.
statements.gap: Zaffalon et al. give local credal constraints and Chen and Darwiche prune zero circuit branches, but neither proves query-independent sufficiency and uniqueness of this support saturation.
statements.consumer: The maximal chart is the finite domain on which the tensor identifier and every nonidentification witness are certified.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\) and every district \(j\), \(B_j\theta_j|_{T_j(S)}=t_j(P_{\theta})\). Moreover, for \(\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_S\), \(P_{\theta}=P_{\theta'}\) if and only if \(B_j\theta_j|_{T_j(S)}=B_j\theta'_j|_{T_j(S)}\) for every \(j\). Every ratio defining \(t_j(P)\) is positive and well defined for every \(P\in\operatorname{relint}(\Delta(S))\).
statements.justification: Positive-prefix telescoping converts the multilinear observational map into separate identified linear signatures.
statements.gap: Hwang et al. provide zero-aware \(Q\)-factor cancellation and Zaffalon et al. provide rootwise credal constraints, but the exact-support fiber equivalence on the maximal chart is not stated in either source.
statements.consumer: It reduces same-law comparison from a nonlinear product fiber to finite rational linear algebra district by district.

statements.statement: If \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\in\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\), then a rational vector \(\lambda\) satisfying \(\lambda B=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\) exists and \(\tau_{x,y}(\theta)=F_{\lambda}(P_{\theta})\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\). The expression has a rational-coefficient numerator over a denominator dividing \(D_S(P)\), and \(D_S(P)>0\) throughout \(\operatorname{relint}(\Delta(S))\).
statements.justification: Success must yield one evaluable formula valid everywhere on the face, not a numerical singleton test.
statements.gap: Arithmetic-circuit invariant cuts and credal singleton computations are instance certificates; the common denominator and face-wide rational identity are the additional output here.
statements.consumer: The functional can be evaluated, differentiated, audited symbolically, and passed to a support-scoped identification engine.

statements.statement: If \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\notin\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\), then there exist \(\theta^+,\theta^-\in\Theta_S\) with rational coordinates, \(\theta_j^+(r_j)>0\) and \(\theta_j^-(r_j)>0\) for every \(j\) and every \(r_j\in T_j(S)\), such that \(P_{\theta^+}=P_{\theta^-}\) and \(\tau_{x,y}(\theta^+)\ne\tau_{x,y}(\theta^-)\). The pair may be chosen to differ in exactly one district law.
statements.justification: The converse must preserve independence, strict positivity on the active chart, exact support, and exact equality of the observational law.
statements.gap: Classical hedges need not preserve a prescribed zero pattern, while polynomial and credal optimization need not emit exact symbolic interior twins.
statements.consumer: Every failure certificate becomes a reproducible pair of finite SCMs rather than an optimizer's nonsingleton interval.

statements.statement: The query \(\tau_{x,y}\) is uniformly identified on the exact support face, meaning \(\tau_{x,y}(\theta)=\tau_{x,y}(\theta')\) for all \(\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_S\) with \(P_{\theta}=P_{\theta'}\), if and only if \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\in\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^m\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B_j)\).
statements.justification: This is the complete theorem-level kernel: a finite support-only criterion with both formula and failure semantics.
statements.gap: The closest papers provide sufficient positivity conditions, invariant cuts, or numerical singleton tests; none gives this support-uniform iff tensor characterization.
statements.consumer: It decides whether a deterministic intervention remains learnable under structural zeros without changing the estimand.

statements.statement: The tensor criterion has the following reductions. For \((G_{\mathrm{bow}},S_{\mathrm{diag}})\), it rejects identification of \(P_{\operatorname{do}(X=1)}(Y=1)\). For \((G_{\mathrm{IV}},S_{\mathrm{IV5}})\), it identifies \(P_{\operatorname{do}(X=0)}(Y=1)=P(X=0,Y=1\mid Z=1)\). When \(S=\mathcal X_V\), every classically identified query is accepted and the rational functional agrees with the classical identifying functional on positive laws.
statements.justification: These controls prevent factual equalities or unsupported cancellations from masquerading as intervention identities.
statements.gap: The five-cell identity and diagonal-bow rejection are not supplied by formula-level positivity checks as a paired completeness diagnostic.
statements.consumer: They provide minimal regression tests for any implementation and recover the familiar full-support regime.

statements.statement: Fix a successful certificate \(\lambda\). In the saturated multinomial model on \(S\), \(\phi_P\) is the efficient influence function of \(F_{\lambda}(P)\). Under independent multinomial sampling, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{S,\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\), \(\sqrt N\{\widehat\tau_N-F_{\lambda}(P)\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{k=1}^N\phi_P(O_k)+o_P(1)\), the studentized statistic converges uniformly to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the plug-in variance \(\sum_{s\in S}\widehat P_N(s)\phi_{\widehat P_N}(s)^2\) is uniformly consistent. On the compatible submodel this gives Wald inference for \(\tau_{x,y}\).
statements.justification: A complete symbolic identifier becomes statistically usable once its rational output has face-tangent inference.
statements.gap: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive graph-native influence functions for important functional classes, but not for arbitrary rational outputs created by exact-support identification on a lower-dimensional multinomial face.
statements.consumer: Analysts with known structural zeros obtain standard errors and confidence intervals without replacing the deterministic intervention target.

statements.statement: Does the support-scoped compiler handle yield a finite do-search calculus that is sound and complete for \(\tau_{x,y}\) over \(\Theta_S\), permits signed intermediate expressions without invalid cancellation, and normalizes every successful derivation to a bounded certificate \(\lambda B=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\) whose denominators divide \(D_S(P)\)? Establish termination, rule-by-rule soundness, completeness relative to the tensor criterion, and an explicit certificate-size bound, or exhibit the first finite counterexample.
statements.justification: The unresolved content is whether product-preserving signed search rules can realize the complete semantic criterion without materializing the full response tensor.
statements.gap: Do-search inherits completeness only from its underlying calculus, and positivity-aware work does not compile structural-zero gains into tensor-normal certificates.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives a support-aware extension of do-search with independently checkable success and failure receipts.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed observational law \(P\) on the known face \(\Delta(S)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query fixes \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\); treatment assignment is not randomized by the sampling design.
sampling_model.overlap: Every supported cell is bounded below by \(\epsilon\); forbidden cells remain structural zeros.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only multinomial cell probabilities are estimated by \(\widehat P_N\); the graph, exact support, and successful rational certificate are treated as supplied.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.1 identifies or zeros a district \(Q\)-factor under specified positive-prefix conditions.
Theorem 2 maps quasi-Markovian observational constraints to exact separate credal sets for the latent roots.
Theorem 4 represents compatible quasi-Markovian functional SCMs exactly by a credal network.
Theorem 1 returns sharp extrema of a discrete causal query through a canonical polynomial program.
Theorem 1 shows the arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut method is at least as complete as classical identification under strict positivity.
Proposition 8 shows variable-state cardinality constraints alone do not improve semi-Markovian identification.
Theorems 2--3 make do-search sound and complete in domains already completely characterized by do-calculus.
Theorem 8 derives the efficient influence function for a graph-derived functional under primal fixability.

tldr: Exact structural zeros are treated as identifying information rather than as failed overlap. In a finite acyclic canonical SCM with one independent response root per bidirected-clique district, first-forbidden-prefix saturation produces the unique maximal Cartesian response support compatible with the supplied realizable observational support. Positive-prefix telescoping recovers linear district signatures. A deterministic intervention query is uniformly identified on the support face exactly when its response indicator lies in the tensor product of those signature row spaces. Membership yields one denominator-safe rational functional; nonmembership yields strictly positive rational same-support, same-law SCM twins with distinct causal answers. The rational output has direct multinomial influence-function inference on fixed interiors, while a sound-and-complete support-scoped do-search normalization remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing work either checks positivity for a formula, certifies selected constrained instances, or numerically optimizes over compatible response laws. It does not give a necessary-and-sufficient support-only criterion uniform over every same-law model on a realizable exact support face.
project_justification.niche: Independent district roots turn observational zeros into a maximal product support and turn supported prefix ratios into separately identified linear signatures. This creates a finite tensor geometry not exposed by full-support do-calculus or generic polynomial optimization.
project_justification.fill: The project proves support saturation, signature recovery, the tensor iff theorem, a rational formula-or-rational-twins dichotomy, and fixed-face multinomial inference, then asks whether signed product-preserving search rules can compile the semantic criterion without enumerating the full tensor.

related_work: Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee supply the writing model: strict positivity fails, positive prefixes can still license \(Q\)-factor operations, and a complete data-adaptive identifier remains unresolved. Zaffalon, Antonucci, and Cabañas, together with their 2024 journal extension, supply the closest method model: quasi-Markovian observations induce separate linear credal constraints and counterfactual bounds follow by credal inference. Their rootwise linearization is treated as established groundwork, while maximal support and the face-uniform symbolic formula-or-twins criterion are the proposed delta. Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser justify canonical finite response types and exact polynomial optimization; Shridharan and Iyengar show how district factorization reduces multilinear degree. Chen and Darwiche show that constrained identifiability can exploit circuit invariants and also clarify that mere state-cardinality restrictions do not create the joint-support information used here. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen provide the search-state and rule-soundness exemplar for the open compiler question. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser provide the differentiation template for converting an identified graphical functional into influence-function inference.
technical_internal_limitation: The semantic tensor criterion permits signed rational coefficients and may require contractions that are not expressible in the current prose grammar of support-scoped probability rules. The core therefore does not claim a complete symbolic compiler. It also treats the exact support mask as known; sampling-zero discrimination and local asymptotics across a changing support remain separate problems.
honest_scope: The support saturation, district-signature recovery, rational success certificate, rational interior failure certificate, tensor iff characterization, destructive controls, and fixed-face multinomial inference are theorem claims to be proved. The do-search normalization is explicitly open. The model class has one mutually independent finite root for each bidirected-clique district and does not include overlapping independent latent-parent neighborhoods. Under full support, the criterion must accept every classically identified query and its functional must agree with the classical answer; the diagonal bow and five-cell instrumental-variable controls test the structural-zero boundary. Support recovery, optimized bit complexity, and empirical software integration are outside scope.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--2, Theorem 5.1 on p. 7, Section 7.2, and the Conclusion on p. 9 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace formula-specific positive-prefix cancellation by a support-global response-type saturation and then test constancy on every same-law fiber.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\text{structural zeros}+\text{causal identification}+\text{response types}+\text{tensor row span}\) and \(\text{quasi-Markovian}+\text{exact support}\) found numerical credal and polynomial programs but no face-uniform tensor criterion.
seed_details.kernel: For every realizable support face in the finite independent-district-root class, uniform identification of \(P_x(y)\) is equivalent to membership of its intervention-response indicator in the tensor product of support-restricted district-signature row spaces.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Hwang et al. because Theorem 5.1 already recovers zero-aware district factors.
seed_details.rebuttal: Theorem 5.1 is a sufficient, formula-local cancellation result and expressly leaves necessity and positivity-aware identification open; it neither constructs the maximal response support nor proves a face-uniform converse.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--2, the strictly positive empirical-law convention and local linear constraints on pp. 5--8, Theorem 2, and the Conclusion on p. 11 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace conditional constraints at every parent configuration by deletion at the first supported prefix whose extension is forbidden.
seed_details.destination_search: The support-saturation and quasi-Markovian credal-network search found no theorem giving a unique largest Cartesian response support for an arbitrary realizable exact support mask.
seed_details.kernel: First-forbidden-prefix deletion is necessary and sufficient for the unique maximal product of district response supports compatible with a realizable observational support face.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate zero propagation from Algorithm 2 of Zaffalon et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: Zero propagation gives necessity; the nonlocal sufficiency that every surviving cross-district tuple remains inside the support, and hence uniqueness of a largest Cartesian chart, is not in that algorithm.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, canonical response construction in Section 3, Proposition 2 and Theorem 1 in Section 4, and the critiques and future-work sections were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace numerical extrema of a multilinear same-law fiber by a rational null-space perturbation that stays in the positive product simplex.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact-witness search found classical hedge witnesses and numerical sharp bounds, but no universal strictly positive rational same-support pair tied to failure of a support-restricted tensor criterion.
seed_details.kernel: Every failed tensor certificate has two rational product response laws, positive on the same maximal supports, with the same exact-support observational law and distinct query values.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary separation does not preserve the nonlinear product parameterization, exact observational support, strict positivity, or rationality; the required one-root perturbation and other-root spanning argument supplies all four.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--2, the search-state construction, Theorems 2--3 on pp. 16--17, and the Conclusion on p. 36 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to attach exact-support domains and signed product certificates to every search state before applying probability transformations.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search located positivity-aware formula checking and context-specific search calculi, but no complete rule system normalizing support-face derivations to bounded tensor certificates.
seed_details.kernel: A finite support-indexed rule system is sound and complete for the declared model class and every successful derivation normalizes to a denominator-safe tensor certificate.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a software extension of do-search.
seed_details.rebuttal: The contribution would be a calculus-level completeness and normalization theorem for signed product expressions, not an implementation feature.
seed_details.disposition: kept as the first-class open question because the normalization proof remains unresolved

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Proposition 1, Section 4 and Proposition 8, Theorems 1--2, and the concluding empirical section were inspected. The paper's state constraints specify variable cardinalities; the first changed step is to condition instead on the exact support of the observational law and propagate its forbidden cells through independent district response types.
seed_details.destination_search: The search confirmed that the 2025 result rules out gains from cardinality information alone, not gains from a supplied exact observational support face.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize exactly when an observational support constraint adds identification beyond a graph, separating mere state-cardinality restrictions from exact-law support restrictions.
seed_details.red_team: Contradicted by Chen and Darwiche because state constraints alone do not improve identification.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their state constraint fixes which values a variable can take, while the proposed object fixes which joint observational cells have positive mass; these are different restrictions, and the theorem would state their boundary explicitly.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it is a corollary-level framing of the tensor kernel

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--3, Theorem 8 and its pathwise-differentiation proof, and the Conclusion on p. 36 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace a fixed positive ADMG law by a triangular multinomial sequence approaching a face where the identifying functional itself changes.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found influence-function theory for graph-derived functionals and overlap-robust alternative interventions, but not a local asymptotic experiment across an identification-changing support boundary.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the Gaussian, weak-denominator, and support-switching limits of a rational support-face estimator as the smallest licensed prefix probability tends to zero.
seed_details.red_team: Routine delta method under weak overlap.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the boundary the support mask and hence the identification criterion changes, so the local experiment is not a fixed-functional weak-overlap calculation.
seed_details.disposition: deferred because the changing-support experiment requires a separate paper

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The sharp polynomial-program theorem and the paper's confidence-region construction were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace a fixed exact support mask by a confidence family of masks and optimize the tensor criterion across that family.
seed_details.destination_search: No located paper combines sampling uncertainty about structural zeros with graph-native sharp bounds over support masks.
seed_details.kernel: Construct valid and, where attainable, sharp causal bounds when observed zero cells may be sampling zeros, using a confidence set over support faces.
seed_details.red_team: Already covered by adding multinomial confidence constraints to autobounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: That construction is available as a generic polynomial program, but an explicit union-of-faces certificate and uniform coverage result would still differ; the likely gain is computational rather than foundational.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because the novelty delta is narrower than the complete-identification kernel

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Definitions 2--3, the arithmetic-circuit construction, Theorem 1 and its Appendix proof, the fixed-distribution examples, and the Conclusion were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace sufficient invariant cuts for a fixed numerical law by a symbolic invariant test uniform over a support face.
seed_details.destination_search: The circuit literature contains sufficient invariant-cut certificates, but the searched sources do not give a face-uniform necessary-and-sufficient symbolic test.
seed_details.kernel: An arithmetic circuit for a causal query is constant on every compatible fiber over a support face if and only if its multilinear coefficient tensor lies in the supported district row span.
seed_details.red_team: A restatement of constrained identifiability in circuit notation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The iff coefficient test and uniform symbolic functional would be new, but this framing is algebraically equivalent to the selected tensor seed and therefore not a distinct angle.
seed_details.disposition: merged into the selected seed rather than counted as a separate contribution

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Theorem 4.1 and proof, and the Conclusion were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace objective-degree reduction by a rank computation exploiting the number and response width of intervened districts.
seed_details.destination_search: The adjacent complexity literature gives multilinear-program degree reductions and NP-hardness, but no output-sensitive complexity bound for support-face tensor certificates.
seed_details.kernel: Bound certificate construction by the intervened-district response width without materializing the full Kronecker matrix.
seed_details.red_team: A standard sparse Kronecker linear-algebra implementation result.
seed_details.rebuttal: A genuine fixed-parameter tractability theorem might survive, but the present evidence does not yet separate it from routine tensor contraction.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after the red-team objection remained unresolved

literature_map.settled: Hwang et al. derive sufficient positivity conditions for given formulas, a zero-aware \(Q\)-factor cancellation theorem, and a sound identifier that reports its required positivity condition.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their Section 7.2 leaves a data-adaptive positivity-aware identifier and necessity unresolved; no support-face-uniform converse is supplied.

literature_map.settled: Chen and Darwiche give sufficient arithmetic-circuit invariant cuts under logical, functional, context-specific, and fixed-law constraints; their later granularity paper proves that state-cardinality restrictions alone do not improve classical identification.
literature_map.open_boundary: Neither paper characterizes constancy uniformly over every compatible law in the relative interior of a prescribed joint observational support face. Exact joint support is not the state-cardinality object ruled out by their proposition.

literature_map.settled: Zaffalon et al. map quasi-Markovian SCM compatibility to separate linear credal sets; the 2020 analysis assumes a strictly positive empirical law, and the 2024 Theorem 4 gives the exact updated credal-network representation and computational bounds.
literature_map.open_boundary: The inspected results do not state a query-independent maximal response-support product, a symbolic tensor singleton criterion over an arbitrary exact support face, or rational interior nonidentification twins.

literature_map.thread: canonical response types and multilinear programs
literature_map.settled: Duarte et al. prove exact canonical finite response reductions and sharp polynomial programs. Shridharan and Iyengar reduce objective degree to the number of intervened districts.
literature_map.open_boundary: These are optimization characterizations; they do not isolate a support-only singleton row-span theorem or symbolic rational twins for every failed query.

literature_map.settled: Do-search is sound and complete in settings whose underlying calculus is complete, while context-specific search adds sound rules beyond ordinary do-calculus.
literature_map.open_boundary: A complete exact-support calculus must preserve product domains, admit signed intermediate arrays, and normalize success to a bounded certificate; that compiler theorem remains open here.

literature_map.settled: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive influence functions and efficient estimators for broad hidden-variable graphical functionals.
literature_map.open_boundary: For a fixed finite support face, a rational compiled functional admits a direct multinomial tangent-space calculation; changing-support nonregularity remains outside the present theorem.
